title: Meditating on Scripture
definition: Meditating on Scripture is the prayerful dwelling of the mind and heart upon God's Word so that its truth is understood, treasured, remembered, and obeyed.
summary: Meditation is not emptying the mind, but filling the heart with God's truth. The believer slowly reflects on Scripture, turns it over in prayer, and allows the Word to shape desires, decisions, worship, and endurance.
christFocus: Christ is the living Word to whom the written Word bears witness. Meditation that is truly biblical leads to deeper trust in Christ, greater dependence upon His grace, and more faithful obedience to His commands.

studySections.heading: Meditation Is Word-Filled Reflection
studySections.content: Biblical meditation is deliberate, reverent, Scripture-shaped reflection. It is not vague spirituality, but the practice of remembering and considering what God has said.

studySections.heading: Meditation Strengthens Obedience
studySections.content: Joshua was commanded to meditate on the law day and night so that he would be careful to do according to it. Meditation helps move truth from the page into the life.

studySections.heading: Meditation Renews the Heart
studySections.content: As the Word dwells richly in the believer, thoughts, desires, fears, and priorities are brought under God's truth. The mind is trained to return to what is true, holy, and faithful.

studySections.heading: Meditation and Prayer
studySections.content: Meditation naturally becomes prayer. The believer may turn Scripture into confession, thanksgiving, praise, repentance, intercession, and surrender.
